relatedWork.title: How I Run an AI Workflow Audit

bodyMarkdown:
Most companies buy AI licenses in a single afternoon and then spend six months wondering why output didn't move. People try a chat window twice, hit one confident wrong answer on a real customer ticket, and go right back to their old spreadsheet.

An Applied AI Enablement Lead fixes that gap. The role sits between operations, engineering, and staff training. Slide-deck workshops alone rarely change daily habits, and hiring a research scientist to fine-tune weights won't fix a messy intake queue. You hire this seat to pick the workflows worth automating, build multi-step pipelines with clear human checkpoints, prove the outputs hold up, and coach non-technical staff until the new process sticks.

## Days 1 to 30: Audit the work and lock a failure baseline

In the first month, I shadow how tickets, documents, and approvals move across desks. Teams usually ask to automate their hardest creative task first. That instinct is understandable, and it almost always stalls out. So we score recurring tasks by weekly volume, error cost, and how fast a person can check a finished draft.

Before writing any agent loop, we pull 25 to 50 real historical examples, including the ugly edge cases that broke past attempts. Those real tickets form our locked test set, and we ship one narrow workflow into daily use before Day 30 so the team sees a working win.

## Days 31 to 60: Wire self-checking pipelines and cut token waste

Single-prompt chat habits break as soon as policy rules stack up. In month two, we split fragile mega-prompts into small stages. Python code checks JSON fields, required links, and math rules first. Separate model families grade tone and policy rules before a human reviewer ever opens the queue.

Across 52,167 multi-agent sessions I governed on contract for an AI-education company, code hooks and tiered routing did most of the heavy lifting. You don't need a frontier reasoning call to check whether a date is missing. Routing simple checks to code and lightweight models kept one 23,740-call run down to $17 total spend with zero false passes.

## Days 61 to 90: Train leads and hand over regression checks

A workflow isn't finished while I'm the only person who can run or debug it. My training is an MA in Applied Linguistics paired with fifteen years leading learning systems, so month three focuses on plain playbooks, clear escalation rules, and live practice labs.

Every team lead gets a short checklist showing when to trust the queue, when to override it, and how to log a bad output. When a vendor swaps a model checkpoint next quarter, the test suite runs overnight and flags drift before morning standup.

## What to test before you hire for this seat

Skip generic brainteasers. Hand the candidate one messy process from your backlog and ask which step stays human, how they catch a model grading its own mistakes, and how they'll teach an ops manager to run it on Monday morning. You can test your open role description right now in the [live 3-model JD diagnostic](/#diagnostic) or [commission a free custom team prototype](/#commission-prototype).

title: Enterprise AI Workflow Audit Checklist: Ranking Tasks by Payoff, Risk & Checkpoints
summary: A practical four-step checklist for auditing team operations before writing automation code: mapping real inputs, pricing silent errors, placing human checkpoints, and killing low-payoff pilots early.
keywords: human in the loop workflow design
bodyMarkdown:
When an operations pilot stalls, the team almost always blames the model. Then you look at the workflow and realize nobody agreed on what a good output looked like before they wired the API.

A real AI workflow audit takes two or three days. Six-week slide decks just delay the real test. I run four plain checks to separate the tasks that pay back right away from the ones that will burn senior review hours.

## Step 1: Pull actual desk inputs from last Tuesday

Ask a team how a process works and they'll describe the clean version from their onboarding doc. Ask to see ten real tickets from Tuesday afternoon and you'll find missing fields, half-pasted screenshots, and three Slack overrides.

Pull twenty real inputs before touching a prompt. When half the tickets lack a customer ID or policy version, a model will guess to fill the blank. Fix the intake form or add a Python pre-check first.

## Step 2: Score tasks on check speed and error cost

I score every candidate task on two simple numbers: how long it takes a person to check the draft, and what breaks if a wrong detail slips out the door.

High-volume tasks that take three hours to write and thirty seconds to verify against a source table pay off right away. Rare tasks that take twenty minutes to fact-check line by line save zero time once you count rework. Leave those manual and move on.

## Step 3: Build the human checkpoint as a decision packet

Saying a human sits in the loop means very little if the reviewer stares at a 900-word AI draft after lunch, because reviewer fatigue sets in by item six and people start clicking approve on autopilot.

Give the reviewer a compact decision packet instead of a wall of prose. Show the exact source quote, list the two policy checks that passed in code, and highlight the single gray-area clause that needs a human call. Reviewers stay sharp when you ask for one clear call.

## Step 4: Set a fail-closed rule before launch

Every step needs a hard rule for what happens when a model cuts off mid-sentence, breaks JSON, or disagrees with a second checker. In my [88,000-call telemetry audit](/work/telemetry-gates/), 324 responses hit unflagged length limits while returning normal HTTP 200 codes. Without code gates checking `finish_reason` and schema fields, broken work looks identical to finished work.

Want to score one of your own team bottlenecks right now? Paste it into the [live workflow diagnostic](/#diagnostic) on the home page.

faqs.q: How long should an enterprise AI workflow audit take?
faqs.a: A focused AI workflow audit for one department takes two to five days: pulling 20 to 50 real historical inputs, scoring tasks by verification speed and error cost, defining human decision packets, and running a small baseline harness.

faqs.q: Why do human-in-the-loop AI workflows still ship mistakes?
faqs.a: Reviewers rubber-stamp long AI drafts when everything looks fluent. Effective human checkpoints present a structured decision packet that highlights source evidence and isolates the exact judgment call required.

faqs.q: What makes a workflow a bad fit for AI automation?
faqs.a: Tasks that happen rarely, lack verifiable source ground truth, or take a senior staff member just as long to fact-check as to write from scratch rarely pay back automation effort.

title: Self-Reviewing Agentic Workflows: Designing Pipelines Non-Technical Teams Trust
summary: How to replace fragile single-shot prompts with four-stage self-checking workflows: deterministic Python pre-gates, narrow drafting nodes, cross-family critics, and SHA-verified audit receipts.
bodyMarkdown:
Give one model a twelve-rule prompt and ask it to research, write, format, and self-grade in a single pass. It will follow nine rules, drop three, and tell you it nailed all twelve.

Self-reviewing workflows fix that by separating the builder from the inspector, using four tight stages and a hard retry cap instead of five chat agents arguing in an open loop.

## Stage 1: Clean intake and pinned source IDs

Python code checks the input file first. Before any model runs, the script strips extra noise and tags every source paragraph with a fixed ID, so later code checks can verify in one millisecond whether a cited paragraph actually exists.

## Stage 2: Narrow drafting steps

Each step does one job. One node pulls dates and dollar amounts into JSON, while the next writes the customer note from that verified record. Narrow steps let you run fast, cheap models on routine work and save heavy models for hard calls.

## Stage 3: Code hooks first, second-family critic next

Never pay an LLM to count words or check JSON keys. Fast Python hooks run first, and in my own pipelines 30+ hook gates catch structural bugs right away at zero token cost.

Once code checks pass, a critic model from a separate vendor grades the draft against a yes/no checklist. Say Claude wrote the draft. Gemini or Llama checks it cold. When the critic spots a miss, it sends back the exact broken rule for one repair pass, and a second miss halts the item for human review.

## Stage 4: Replayable SHA-256 receipts

Ops leaders trust what they can inspect. Every run logs the input hash, model version, hook results, critic scores, and final diff into a single `.jsonl` receipt, so when someone asks why an item shipped last Thursday, you open that file and replay every step in two seconds.

You can read runnable code in my [self-reviewing workflow demo](/work/agentic-workflow-demo/) or [request a free custom 4-stage prototype](/#commission-prototype) built around your stack.

faqs.q: Why shouldn't the same LLM review its own output?
faqs.a: Models share blindspots with their own weights and training style. When a model grades its own draft, it routinely overlooks hallucinations and rubric misses that a separate model family catches right away.

faqs.q: How many retry loops should a self-reviewing workflow allow?
faqs.a: Cap automated repair loops at one or two retries with structured defect feedback. Beyond two retries, models often game the rubric or degrade good sections, so unresolved items should fail closed to a human queue.

faqs.q: How do non-technical teams monitor multi-agent workflows?
faqs.a: Plain status dashboards backed by JSONL audit receipts show pass rates, blocked items, token cost per item, and clean side-by-side diffs whenever human approval is needed.

title: LLM-as-a-Judge Calibration: Stopping Self-Bias, Verdict Flips & Silent Truncations
summary: How to calibrate LLM-as-a-Judge panels against human expert baselines: binary decomposed rubrics, cross-vendor panels, golden-set agreement checks, and catching silent HTTP 200 truncations.

relatedWork.title: Why LLM Output Gets Cut Off Silently

bodyMarkdown:
Teams love LLM-as-a-Judge because human grading is slow. So someone wires a 1-to-5 star prompt onto the same model that wrote the answer. The dashboard shows a 4.7 average on Monday, and customers still complain on Wednesday.

An uncalibrated judge is worse than having no metric at all. It gives broken releases a green badge. Fixing judge trust comes down to four plain habits.

## Swap 1-to-5 star ratings for yes/no facts

Ask a model to rate 'clarity' from 1 to 5 and it will pick 4 almost every time. Worse, swap the order of two bullets in the prompt and the score flips. Break vague ratings into yes/no facts instead. Did the reply cite the policy number? Was any refund tier invented outside the source table? Does the hint give away the answer? Yes/no checks match human experts far more often.

## Split the writer model from the judge panel

Asking the same model five times only proves that it agrees with its own blindspots. In my [multi-model panel tests](/work/multi-model-panels-vs-resampling/) and [judge-trust benchmark](/work/judge-trust/), pairing separate model vendors cut false passes from 5% down to 0.0% on seeded bugs. When two vendors disagree, you know right where to look.

## Check API cutoffs before you grade text

Across 88,000 API calls I audited across twelve models, 324 replies hit `finish_reason = length` or returned empty thinking blocks while reporting HTTP 200 OK. Check stop reasons in Python first so you never pay a judge to grade half a sentence.

## Lock a 50-item human golden set

Before trusting any automated rubric, grade 50 real items yourself across clean passes, borderline calls, and real bugs. Track exact pass/fail match and false-pass rate on that folder. Every time you edit the rubric prompt, re-run those 50 items first to prove the change helped.

See how I apply these checks in a [$4,500 AI Rubric & Exam Hardening Sprint](/hire/).

faqs.q: Why do 1-to-5 LLM judge scores fail in production?
faqs.a: Subjective 1-to-5 scales cluster around 4 and shift when prompt formatting changes. Decomposing rubrics into specific binary pass/fail checks makes verdicts reproducible and auditable.

faqs.q: How big should a golden calibration set be for an LLM judge?
faqs.a: Starting with 30 to 50 real examples labeled by a domain expert, balanced across clear passes, hard edge cases, and realistic defects, is enough to catch high false-pass rates early.

faqs.q: What is false-pass rate in LLM quality control?
faqs.a: False-pass rate is the share of defective outputs that an automated judge mistakenly marks as acceptable. In customer-facing or instructional systems, minimizing false passes matters more than raw average score.

title: SOP-to-SCORM AI Pipeline: Compiling Policy Docs into Verified LMS & QTI Modules
summary: How corporate L&D and compliance teams turn static SOPs and runbooks into ADL SCORM 1.2 packages, QTI 1.2 item banks, 300-DPI guides, and narrated 1080p lessons with 0% policy drift.

relatedWork.title: Interactive SOP-to-LMS Compiler & Sample SCORM Download
Catching Feedback That Leaks the Answer

bodyMarkdown:
Corporate training teams sit on stacks of updated SOPs, security runbooks, and product docs. Turning one policy PDF into an LMS module, a scenario quiz, and a narrated lesson usually takes four to six weeks by hand. Often the software screen changes before the course even ships.

An SOP-to-SCORM compiler treats course builds like a clean code pipeline. You feed in the approved policy doc and get verified training files out the other side in a single day.

## Step 1: Start from real mistakes on the job

Copying policy text onto slides and adding five trivia questions at the end never changes how staff work. Using backward design, the pipeline pulls out the exact mistakes people make under time pressure first. Every scenario question and worked example maps back to a named section in your source SOP.

## Step 2: Run four blind solvers on every quiz item

AI quizzes break in two common ways: either two choices are both right, or an explanation argues against your own policy. Before any question ships, four separate models take the quiz blind using only the source SOP and the question stem.

All four blind solvers have to pick the same key. Split votes drop the item right away, and a fresh question takes its place.

## Step 3: Package clean SCORM 1.2, QTI 1.2 & 1080p video

Once every question passes, Python builds the `imsmanifest.xml` file, wires the SCORM 1.2 score and completion hooks, formats QTI 1.2 quiz banks, lays out 300-DPI print guides, and renders 1080p narrated video with captions.

Test the live SCORM 1.2 sandbox and download a sample `.zip` module at [/sop-to-lms/](/sop-to-lms/). You can also read the [print playbook on Amazon ($24.99)](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HRQFWFPR) or see how I fix grading rubrics at [/hire/](/hire/).

faqs.a: Yes. By pairing structured extraction and blind-solver verification with deterministic XML and JavaScript packagers, an SOP-to-SCORM pipeline emits standards-compliant ADL SCORM 1.2 .zip modules ready for Cornerstone, Docebo, Workday Learning, Moodle, or Canvas.

faqs.a: Every claim and quiz rationale is pinned to an explicit source section in the approved SOP, and four independent blind-solver checks verify that only the keyed answer holds up under policy rules.

title: 6-Rung LLM Cost & Latency Routing: Cutting Enterprise Token Spend Without Losing Quality
summary: Why a tiny fraction of agent calls burn 80% of your API bill, and how a 6-rung policy router shifts routine checks to zero-token Python hooks and fast mid-tier models.

relatedWork.title: Why LLM API Costs Concentrate in Few Calls
How Much Do Reasoning Tokens Really Cost?

bodyMarkdown:
When finance flags a runaway AI bill, teams usually try swapping the whole app onto a tiny model. Quality tanks the same week, product rolls the change back, and everyone assumes high token bills are the cost of doing business.

In real logs, token spend is lopsided. A few giant context loops and unbridled thinking calls burn 80% of the budget, while most traffic just parses fields, routes tags, or checks formatting.

## How the 6-rung router splits the work

Instead of picking one model for the whole product, send each step to the lowest rung that clears your golden test set:

1. **Rung 0 (Zero-token Python hooks):** Regex, AST, JSON schema, URL, word-count, and banned-phrase gates. Instant and free.
2. **Rung 1 (Exact & prompt cache):** Reuse static policy tables and rubric instructions.
3. **Rung 2 (Fast small models):** Field parsing, tag routing, and table cleanup.
4. **Rung 3 (Mid-tier workhorse models):** First-pass drafting and structured summaries.
5. **Rung 4 (Two-vendor critic pair):** Separate mid-tier models grading yes/no rubric checks.
6. **Rung 5 (Frontier reasoning escalation):** Saved strictly for hard synthesis or tie-breaking when Rung 4 critics split.

## What happens to the bill in production

On a 23,740-call run through my open-source routing harness, pushing structural checks to Rung 0 and saving frontier calls for real tie-breakers brought total API spend down to $17 while holding a 0.0% false-pass rate.

Compare live routing cost curves on the [Model Cost & Latency Tribunal](/m5-tribunal/).

faqs.q: How do you cut enterprise LLM API costs without hurting accuracy?
faqs.a: Move structural checks into zero-token Python hooks first, route routine extraction to fast low-cost models, and reserve expensive frontier reasoning models strictly for hard synthesis or split-verdict tie-breakers.

faqs.q: Why do reasoning models blow up production budgets unexpectedly?
faqs.a: Reasoning models emit thousands of hidden thinking tokens even on simple formatting or yes/no checks unless max-token caps and tiered routing rules restrict where reasoning mode is invoked.

faqs.q: How do you verify a cheaper model rung is safe to deploy?
faqs.a: Replay your locked 50-item golden test set across both the frontier baseline and the candidate rung, checking that false-pass rate stays flat and p95 latency improves before switching live traffic.

title: AI Curriculum & QTI Assessment Quality Control: Blind-Solver Checks & Zero Answer Leaks
summary: Engineering-grade quality control for EdTech and enterprise assessment pipelines: catching ambiguous distractors, standards drift, hint answer leaks, and broken math rendering before students see them.

relatedWork.title: Do AI Assessment Items Measure What They Claim?
Catching Feedback That Reveals the Answer

bodyMarkdown:
Shipping a weak blog sentence is annoying. Shipping a test question with two right answers or a tutor hint that gives away Choice B wrecks learner trust in thirty seconds.

I spent fifteen years in classrooms and curriculum leadership before building automated instructional pipelines. Later, I governed 52,000+ multi-agent runs on contract for an AI-education company. Fluent prose hides bad teaching unless you test every question like production software.

## Bug 1: Two defensible keys or throwaway wrong choices

Let one model write a multiple-choice item and its own rationale, and it will defend a broken key every time. Blind-solver checks stop that cold. Strip out the key, hand the stem and choices to three separate model vendors, and require all three to pick the exact same answer from scratch.

Good wrong choices aren't random jokes either. Each distractor needs to map to a real mistake learners make on that skill.

## Bug 2: Hints that give away the answer

Practice tutors often show a hint after a wrong first try. Because models aim to please, their hints often repeat the exact words sitting inside Choice C. Run a simple leak test to catch it: show a separate model *only* the hint and the four choices, hiding the question stem. Whenever that blind guesser still nails the right letter, the hint leaked too much.

## Bug 3: Silent drift away from the target standard

Ask a model for a tenth-grade question on a specific skill and it will often test side trivia or write at a graduate reading level. Python readability checks, stimulus rules, and binary skill gates block off-target items before human editors waste hours fixing them.

If your team is scaling curriculum or QTI item banks, test the [live SCORM & QTI verification demo](/sop-to-lms/) or [book a 20-minute scope call](/hire/).

faqs.q: What is blind-solver verification for AI-generated assessments?
faqs.a: Blind-solver verification strips the intended answer key from a generated question and asks independent models to solve it from scratch. If solvers split across two choices or fail to match the key, the item is flagged as ambiguous and blocked.

faqs.q: How do you stop AI tutoring hints from giving away the answer?
faqs.a: Run an answer-leak test where a separate checker sees only the hint and the answer options without the question stem. If the checker can identify the right option from the hint alone, the hint reveals too much and gets rewritten.

faqs.q: Can QTI XML and LMS packaging be validated automatically in CI?
faqs.a: Yes. Deterministic schema validators check QTI XML structure, unique identifiers, math notation balance, and SCORM manifest bindings before any human editorial review begins.
